provenance.editorialMethod: New bounded recognition, word-order and production questions using clear source vocabulary and dialogue forms. Vegetable, fruit and coffee orders reuse the reviewed quantities and service patterns; short answers state their scope and accept equivalent forms where appropriate. These are not the supplied worksheets or teacher-provided answer keys.

items.prompt: Match the vegetables to their English meanings.
items.explanation: Ġidra is kohlrabi, not turnip. Karrotti is the spelling used in the NSO bilingual list.

items.prompt: In the supermarket drinks section, what does minerali mean?
items.explanation: Minerali refers to soft drinks in this shopping context, not mineral substances.

items.prompt: Write the Maltese phrase for half a kilo (before perżut).
items.explanation: Nofs kilo perżut means half a kilo of ham.

items.prompt: Which quantity means 300 grams of bacon?
items.explanation: Tliet mitt gramma is 300 grams; mitejn gramma is 200 grams.

items.prompt: The assistant asks Xi ħaġa oħra? Your shopping list is complete. Choose the reply.
items.explanation: Dak kollox closes the order: that is all.

items.prompt: Write the Maltese phrase for grated cheese.
items.explanation: Ġobon maħkuk is grated cheese.

items.prompt: Match each milk choice to its meaning.
items.explanation: These are different milk choices; ħalib tal-lewż is almond milk.

items.prompt: Write the phrase meaning without sugar, beginning with mingħajr.
items.explanation: Mingħajr zokkor means without sugar.

items.prompt: Sara addresses one waiter. Which form of please fits?
items.explanation: Choose the form for the recipient: Sara is addressing one person.

items.prompt: A waiter addresses Sara and Rita together. Which phrase means I will be with you shortly?
items.explanation: Magħkom refers to more than one person being addressed, even though only one waiter is speaking.

items.prompt: In Rita's café order, what does pasta bil-krema taċ-ċikkulata mean?
items.explanation: Pasta means a pastry in this café context.

items.prompt: Which sentence says I will pay in cash?
items.explanation: Bi flus kontanti means in cash; bil-karta means by card.

items.prompt: Your list says a cabbage and a kilo of carrots. Which order matches it?
choices: Għandi bżonn kaboċċa u kilo karrotti.
Għandi bżonn pastarda u kilo karrotti.
Għandi bżonn kaboċċa u kilo tuffieħ.
items.answer: Għandi bżonn kaboċċa u kilo karrotti.
items.explanation: Kaboċċa is a cabbage; kilo karrotti is a kilo of carrots.

reviewCard.maltese: Għandi bżonn kaboċċa u kilo karrotti.
reviewCard.english: I need a cabbage and a kilo of carrots.

items.prompt: Match the vegetables on the counter to the shopping list.
items.explanation: These are the produce names used on this page; ħassa names one lettuce.

items.prompt: You also need garlic. Complete only the missing noun: Għandi bżonn ftit ___.
items.explanation: Għandi bżonn ftit tewm means I need some garlic.

reviewCard.english: I need some garlic.

items.prompt: Order a cabbage. Begin with Nixtieq and put please at the end.
items.explanation: Nixtieq makes the request; jekk jogħġbok addresses one shop assistant.

reviewCard.english: I would like a cabbage, please.

items.prompt: You need half a kilo of potatoes, not a whole kilo. Choose the order.
items.explanation: Nofs kilo is half a kilo; patata means potatoes here.

reviewCard.english: I would like half a kilo of potatoes.

items.prompt: Complete only the measure for a kilo of carrots: Nixtieq ___ karrotti.
items.explanation: Kilo karrotti means a kilo of carrots; kilogramma is also accepted for the measure.

items.prompt: The assistant asks Xi ħaġa oħra? Add a lettuce, beginning with U and ending with please.
items.explanation: U ħassa adds a lettuce to the order already in progress.

reviewCard.english: And a lettuce, please.

items.prompt: Your order is complete. Write only the two-word phrase meaning that is all: ___. Grazzi.
items.explanation: Dak kollox. Grazzi. closes the order politely.

reviewCard.english: That is all. Thank you.

items.prompt: Match the fruit in your order to its English meaning.
items.explanation: These fruit names are reused with measures such as kilo, ftit and żewġ kaxxi.

items.prompt: Order one kilo of apples and two kilograms of oranges. Which list is correct?
choices: kilo larinġ u żewġ kilogrammi tuffieħ
żewġ kilogrammi tuffieħ u kilo larinġ
kilo tuffieħ u żewġ kilogrammi larinġ
items.answer: kilo tuffieħ u żewġ kilogrammi larinġ
items.explanation: Check both the fruit and its quantity: one kilo of apples, two kilograms of oranges.

reviewCard.maltese: Għandi bżonn kilo tuffieħ u żewġ kilogrammi larinġ.
reviewCard.english: I need a kilo of apples and two kilograms of oranges.

items.prompt: Order a kilo of apples. Begin with Nixtieq and put please at the end.
items.explanation: The measure kilo comes before the fruit name tuffieħ.

reviewCard.english: I would like a kilo of apples, please.

items.prompt: Write two kilograms, using kilogrammi: Għandi bżonn ___ larinġ.
items.explanation: Żewġ kilogrammi larinġ is the two-kilogram orange order in the model.

items.prompt: Complete only the word for some / a little: U ___ għeneb, jekk jogħġbok.
items.explanation: Ftit għeneb means some grapes.

reviewCard.english: And some grapes, please.

items.prompt: The strawberries are sold in boxes. Which order asks for two boxes?
items.explanation: Żewġ kaxxi means two boxes; the unit is boxes, not kilograms.

reviewCard.english: I will take two boxes of strawberries.

items.prompt: Ask how much the two boxes cost. Begin with Kemm and put please at the end.
items.explanation: Kemm huma? asks how much they cost in this shopping context.

reviewCard.english: How much are they, please?

items.prompt: You have paid. The assistant says Il-ġurnata t-tajba! Choose the reply meaning you too.
items.explanation: Lilek ukoll returns the good wish to one person.

reviewCard.english: You too.

items.prompt: You want black coffee without sugar. Choose the matching order.
items.explanation: Iswed specifies black coffee; mingħajr zokkor excludes sugar.

reviewCard.english: I would like black coffee without sugar.

items.prompt: The barista asks about milk. Match the options to their meanings.
items.explanation: Tal-ħafur is oat; tal-lewż is almond. These are different milk choices.

items.prompt: Order coffee with milk. Begin with Nixtieq and put please at the end.
items.explanation: Bil-ħalib means with milk.

reviewCard.english: I would like coffee with milk, please.

items.prompt: Write one word meaning without: Nixtieq kafè ___ zokkor.
items.explanation: Both mingħajr zokkor and bla zokkor mean without sugar.

reviewCard.english: I would like coffee without sugar.

items.prompt: The barista asks Hawnhekk jew take-away? You want to take the coffee away. Choose the reply.
items.explanation: Take-away answers where you want the order, not how you will pay.

reviewCard.english: To take away, please.

items.prompt: Complete only the Maltese drink name for cappuccino: Nixtieq ___, jekk jogħġbok.
items.explanation: The Maltese spelling used in the coffee bank is kapuċċino.

reviewCard.english: I would like a cappuccino, please.

items.prompt: Order a cappuccino with oat milk. Begin with Nixtieq.
items.explanation: Bil-ħalib tal-ħafur specifies with oat milk, rather than almond or dairy milk.

reviewCard.english: I would like a cappuccino with oat milk.

items.prompt: The barista offers white or brown sugar. Which phrase selects brown sugar?
items.explanation: Zokkor ismar is brown sugar; zokkor abjad is white sugar.

reviewCard.english: Brown sugar, please.

items.prompt: You address one barista. Complete only the missing word: Nixtieq espresso, jekk ___.
items.explanation: Jekk jogħġbok addresses one person. Use jogħġobkom when addressing more than one.

reviewCard.english: I would like an espresso, please.

items.prompt: Your order is ready and you want to ask whether you can pay by card. Choose the question.
items.explanation: This asks whether card payment is possible. Bi flus kontanti means in cash.

reviewCard.english: Can I pay by card?
